items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: New York Times interview (published January 8, as quoted by Reuters)
items.quote: I have in my mind a decision
items.summary: Trump told the New York Times on Wednesday night that he had made up his mind on the next Fed Chair but had not discussed it with anybody; he called Hassett 'certainly one of the people that I like'. Reported by Reuters in a story on Bessent's Minnesota remarks.
items.score_note: Fed Chair selection only; no policy-rate content.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post ordering $200 billion of mortgage bond purchases
items.quote: This will drive Mortgage Rates DOWN, monthly payments DOWN, and make the cost of owning a home more affordable.
items.summary: Trump said he is instructing his representatives (using Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac cash) to buy $200 billion of mortgage bonds to push mortgage rates down. No statement about the Fed's policy rate. Source is the trumpstruth.org archive, which reproduces the post in full.
items.score_note: About mortgage rates via GSE purchases, not the Fed's policy rate; no usable Fed-path content.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Remarks before the Economic Club of Minnesota
items.quote: at a certain point, the Federal Reserve must also do its part to spur investment.
items.summary: In prepared remarks Bessent said the White House can only do so much and the Fed must do its part to spur investment. He said the Fed needs 'merely an open mind' and cited Greenspan resisting premature rate hikes in the 1990s tech boom. In Q&A he said a Fed Chair decision was likely later in January (Reuters).
items.score_note: The text posted on treasury.gov says the Fed 'must also do its part'. Press reports of the remarks released that day (CNBC, relayed at themortgagepoint.com/2026/01/08/treasury-secretary-more-fed-rate-cuts-are-only-ingredient-missing-for-stronger-economy/) quote him: 'Cutting interest rates ... is the only ingredient missing ... Which is why the Fed should not delay.' That wording is not in the posted text. Scored -2 on the explicit call for cuts; would be -1 on the posted text alone.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Reuters interview, Savage, Minnesota
items.quote: So I think the idea is to roughly match the Fed, which has been pushing the other way.
items.summary: Bessent told Reuters the administration's $200 billion of Fannie/Freddie MBS purchases is meant to roughly offset the about $15 billion a month of MBS rolling off the Fed's balance sheet. He said the purchases would lower mortgage rates only indirectly, through the MBS spread over Treasuries.
items.score_note: About offsetting the Fed's MBS run-off through GSE purchases; no statement on the policy rate path.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle aboard Air Force One
items.quote: With no help from the Fed, because we have a total stiff at the Fed.
items.summary: Discussing the $200 billion mortgage bond purchases, Trump said interest rates are falling very rapidly 'with no help from the Fed' and called the Fed Chair 'a total stiff'.
items.score_note: Complains the Fed is not helping rates fall; no explicit cut demand in this exchange.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: NBC News phone interview after Powell disclosed the DOJ subpoenas (as reported by Reuters)
items.quote: I don’t know anything about it, but he’s certainly not very good at the Fed, and he’s not very good at building buildings
items.summary: After Powell disclosed that the Justice Department had threatened him with a criminal indictment, Trump told NBC News he had no knowledge of the action but that Powell is not very good at the Fed or at building buildings.
items.score_note: Reaction to the Powell probe; no statement on what rates should do.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post after December CPI release
items.quote: That means that Jerome “Too Late” Powell should cut interest rates, MEANINGFULLY!!!
items.summary: Reacting to the CPI print, Trump said the low inflation numbers mean Powell should cut rates meaningfully, or he will continue to be 'too late'. He also touted growth numbers and tariffs.
items.score_note: Explicit call for a meaningful rate cut now.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle before Marine One departure (after CPI release)
items.quote: that would give Too Late Powell the chance to give us a nice, beautiful big rate cut
items.summary: Leaving for Detroit after the CPI release, Trump said very low inflation gives Powell the chance to deliver a big rate cut, which would be great for the country.
items.score_note: Explicit call for a big rate cut.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Speech to the Detroit Economic Club
items.quote: our country becomes stronger and therefore interest rates should go down, not up.
items.summary: Trump said the Fed raises rates and kills every rally whenever good numbers are announced, and that he wants a Fed head under whom rates go down when the economy is strong. He called Powell 'a real stiff' and 'that jerk' who 'will be gone soon', and said mortgage rates are falling without the Fed's help.
items.score_note: Says rates should go down, not up, and attacks the Fed for hiking on good news.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks during Ford plant tour, Dearborn, Michigan
items.quote: he's bad because his interest rates were too high.
items.summary: Asked about Senator Tillis's objections to the Powell probe, Trump said 'we have a bad fed chairman' who is bad because his interest rates were too high, and cited that day's inflation and growth reports.
items.score_note: Criticism of rates being too high, phrased in the past tense; no explicit cut demand here.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: CBS News interview with Tony Dokoupil, Dearborn
items.quote: he's been too high on interest rates, and I call him too late.
items.summary: Asked about accusations of pressuring the Fed, Trump called Powell 'a lousy Fed chairman', said he has been too high on interest rates and 'should have reduced' by more, and criticised the Fed building renovation.
items.score_note: Says Powell should have cut more; criticism of past policy rather than an explicit new cut demand.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle after Air Force One arrival
items.quote: We should have lower rates.
items.summary: Asked about Jamie Dimon's warning against chipping away at Fed independence, Trump said Dimon is wrong, that what he is doing is fine, Powell has done a bad job and 'we should have lower rates'.
items.score_note: Explicit statement that rates should be lower, in defence of pressuring the Fed.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Reuters interview in the Oval Office
items.quote: I made a lot of money with business, so I think I have a better understanding of it than Too Late Jerome Powell.
items.summary: Trump said he has no plan to fire Powell despite the DOJ investigation but that it is 'too early' to say, that 'the two Kevins' (Warsh, Hassett) are very good and he would announce a pick in the next couple of weeks, and that 'a president should have something to say' about Fed policy. He said 'I don't care' about criticism that he is eroding Fed independence.
items.score_note: Asserts a presidential say over Fed policy but states no rate direction in the quoted text.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post denying he offered Jamie Dimon the Fed Chair job
items.quote: This statement is totally untrue, there was never such an offer
items.summary: Trump denied a Wall Street Journal report that he had offered Jamie Dimon the Fed Chair job and said he would sue JPMorgan over debanking. No rate-path content.
items.score_note: Fed Chair selection only; no policy-rate content.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview from Davos (Joe Kernen)
items.quote: my prediction is that inflation is going to drop substantially this year
items.summary: Bessent said Trump could decide on the next Fed Chair as soon as next week (four candidates left), called Powell's plan to attend the Supreme Court hearing on Lisa Cook a mistake, and said the Fed loses $100 billion a year from mistimed asset purchases. He argued the US is in a 1990s-style productivity boom, the Fed should keep an open mind and let the economy run, and inflation will drop substantially this year.
items.score_note: Argues against tightening on strong growth and forecasts lower inflation; no explicit call for an immediate cut in this transcript.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: White House press briefing
items.quote: In the old days if you had good numbers, they'd lower interest rates or they wouldn't do anything.
items.summary: Trump said growth could be far higher if the Fed did not raise rates every time there are good numbers, said 'they shouldn't do it', and that the Fed tries to 'kill' success.
items.score_note: Opposes rate hikes in response to strong growth; no explicit cut demand in this passage.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: CNBC interview with Joe Kernen in Davos (aired on Closing Bell)
items.quote: He's always too late, except when it comes to politics for the other side, where he was actually too early.
items.summary: Trump said the Fed Chair shortlist was down to 'maybe one in my mind', praised Hassett, Rieder and the others, and said he wants a Greenspan-like chair who will not raise rates when growth numbers are strong. He said growth is not a big cause of inflation, called Powell always too late, and said Powell's life 'won't be very, very happy' if he stays on as governor.
items.score_note: Clear dovish pressure (Powell too late, do not hike on good numbers) but no explicit 'cut now' in this interview; scored nearer 0.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Special address at the World Economic Forum, Davos
items.quote: we should be paying a much lower interest rate than we are.
items.summary: Trump said he would announce a new Fed chairman 'in the not too distant future', complained that Fed chairs change once they get the job and raise rates, called Powell a terrible chairman who is always too late, and said the US should pay the lowest interest rate of any country.
items.score_note: Explicitly says US rates should be much lower, the lowest in the world.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum, Davos
items.quote: I’m not concerned at all.
items.summary: Asked whether the Greenland dispute could trigger European selling of US Treasuries, Bessent said he was not concerned, called Denmark's Treasury holdings 'irrelevant' and said Treasury auctions have seen record foreign investment.
items.score_note: About foreign demand for Treasuries; no statement on Fed policy.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post on mortgage rates hitting a three-year low
items.quote: The Fed has been hurt and discredited during Too Late’s reign!
items.summary: Trump said mortgage rates hit a three-year low despite Powell's 'never ending quest to keep Interest Rates high', and that the market is overtaking Powell's obstinance.
items.score_note: Attacks Powell for keeping rates high (implied wish for lower rates) without an explicit cut demand in this post.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle aboard Air Force One (return from Davos)
items.quote: Despite that, we have interest rates going down.
items.summary: Asked whether the DOJ investigation might make Powell stay longer at the Fed, Trump said he is not concerned, called Powell 'always too late', and said interest rates are going down despite him.
items.score_note: 'Too late' criticism without an explicit demand in this exchange.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle before Marine One departure (first day of January FOMC)
items.quote: I'd like to see interest rates go down, everything else is going down.
items.summary: Asked how far he would like mortgage rates to drop, Trump said he would like to see interest rates go down, as energy, gasoline and grocery prices are falling.
items.score_note: General wish for lower rates in answer to a mortgage-rate question; not a direct demand on the Fed.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Speech on the economy and energy, Clive, Iowa
items.quote: he wants to keep rates as high as possible.
items.summary: Trump called Powell a bad Fed chairman who is 'too late' and wants to keep rates as high as possible, and said mortgage rates were driven down to a three-year low despite him.
items.score_note: Attacks Powell for keeping rates high; implied wish for lower rates, no explicit cut demand.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk on the Street interview (Sara Eisen), FOMC decision day
items.quote: I do think that there are many members on the board who had a false narrative on inflation
items.summary: Asked whether a hold at that day's FOMC would be a mistake, Bessent said it is up to the Fed but that many board members had a false narrative on inflation and he hopes they keep an open mind over the next couple of months. He said inflation is moving back toward target and there are four great Fed Chair candidates.
items.score_note: Declines to call the hold a mistake but says the Fed's inflation narrative is wrong; leans easier.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post the morning after the January FOMC hold
items.quote: The Fed should substantially lower interest rates, NOW!
items.summary: Trump said Powell 'again refused to cut interest rates' with no reason to keep them high, is hurting the country and national security, and is costing hundreds of billions in interest expense. He said the US should pay the lowest interest rate of any country because of tariff revenue.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for substantially lower rates now.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Cabinet meeting at the White House (day after January FOMC hold)
items.quote: We should have the lowest interest rate anywhere in the world.
items.summary: Trump said the Fed's rates are 'unacceptably high', the US is paying far too much interest and should have the lowest rate in the world. He said he wants a system where good news leads to lower rather than higher rates, that 'if inflation comes, we'll take care of it when it comes', and that the right Fed choice would help get rates down.
items.score_note: Calls Fed rates unacceptably high and demands the lowest rate in the world.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press gaggle at a movie premiere, Washington
items.quote: you notice that the interest rates now are falling despite The Fed.
items.summary: Asked about the 10-2 FOMC vote to hold, Trump said there are 'political people' on the Fed who vote against him, that the Fed could have been much more helpful, and that he would announce his Fed Chair choice the next morning.
items.score_note: Says the Fed should have been more helpful and frames the hold as political; no explicit demand in this exchange.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social posts announcing the nomination of Kevin Warsh as Fed Chair
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that I am nominating Kevin Warsh to be the CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF THE FEDERAL RESERVE SYSTEM.
items.summary: Trump announced Warsh's nomination, said he will 'go down as one of the GREAT Fed Chairmen' and is 'central casting'. In follow-up posts at 07:34 and 07:45 (statuses 36362, 36366) he said he kept Hassett at the White House and praised Waller and Rieder. No rate-path statement in these posts.
items.score_note: Personnel announcement; no policy-rate content in the post text.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office remarks at executive order signing (day of Warsh nomination)
items.quote: But he certainly wants to cut rates.
items.summary: Asked whether Warsh committed to cut rates, Trump said no, that asking would be inappropriate and he wants to keep it 'nice and pure', but that Warsh certainly wants to cut rates. He called Warsh the perfect candidate and 'central casting'.
items.score_note: Expresses expectation that his nominee will cut, while denying he asked for a commitment; scored -1 rather than -2 because no direct demand is made.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office bill-signing remarks (Q&A on the Powell probe)
items.quote: No, she's going to take it to the end and see.
items.summary: Asked whether he would like US Attorney Jeanine Pirro to drop the investigation of Powell to ease Warsh's confirmation, Trump said no, that she will take it to the end, and that the Fed renovation shows gross incompetence or theft.
items.score_note: About the Powell investigation; no policy-rate content.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: NBC News interview with Tom Llamas
items.quote: He would not have gotten the job, no.
items.summary: Asked whether Warsh understands that he wants lower rates, Trump said 'I think he does. But I think he wants to anyway', and confirmed that if Warsh had said he wanted to raise rates he would not have gotten the job. He said US rates are 'way high', inflation is low, and all he has to do now is 'get down the interest rates'. He said the Fed is 'in theory' an independent body.
items.score_note: Makes lower rates a condition for the Fed Chair job and says rates must come down.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: House Financial Services Committee hearing on the FSOC annual report (Q&A)
items.quote: I do believe that the Federal Reserve has to maintain credibility and be like Caesar’s wife, beyond reproach.
items.summary: In Q&A Bessent said he considers the Fed an independent agency but has no opinion on whether a president may fire Fed officials over policy disagreements. He said Fed independence rests on public trust that was lost when it let inflation 'ravage' incomes, that Trump has the right to voice views on rates, and that he was wrong to have called tariffs inflationary. The prepared statement (treasury.gov sb0387) has no monetary-policy content.
items.score_note: Fed independence and credibility only; no statement on what rates should do.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Senate Banking Committee hearing on the FSOC annual report (Q&A)
items.quote: That is up to the president
items.summary: Asked by Senator Warren to promise that Warsh would not be sued or investigated if he does not cut rates the way Trump wants, Bessent replied 'That is up to the president'. The prepared statement (treasury.gov sb0388) has no monetary-policy content.
items.score_note: Declines to rule out legal pressure on the Fed nominee; no statement on the rate path itself.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Halftime Report interview (Scott Wapner), excerpts
items.quote: The President has great respect for the Fed, for the Fed’s independence, and Kevin Warsh is his choice.
items.summary: CNBC published excerpts only. Bessent said Trump respects Fed independence and that Warsh brings credibility and will be a fantastic leader on monetary policy and regulation. On the Powell probe he said 'no crime, but probably guilty of incompetence'. The page header misprints the year as 2025; the body and video link give Friday, February 6, 2026.
items.score_note: No rate-path content in the published excerpts.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Fox News 'Sunday Morning Futures' interview
items.quote: I would think that they’ll probably sit back, take at least a year to decide what they want to do.
items.summary: Bessent said balance sheet decisions are up to the Fed, that he would not expect it to do anything quickly, and that an ample-reserves regime requires a larger balance sheet. He said Warsh will be a very independent Fed chief.
items.score_note: Forecast that the Fed will not shrink its balance sheet quickly; neutral for the rate path.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Fox Business interview with Larry Kudlow
items.quote: We should be two points lower right now.
items.summary: Trump said rates should already have been cut and should be two points lower, that every point costs $600 billion and two points lower would eliminate the deficit, and that the US should have the lowest rates in the world. He said all the new Fed head has to do is lower interest rates and complained that the Fed stops growth by raising rates. Factba.se dates the interview February 9 (the URL slug carries a 2023 typo).
items.score_note: Explicit demand for rates two points lower.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview (as reported by Reuters)
items.quote: anyone who cares about the integrity, the independence of the Fed is going to want to see continuity with Kevin Warsh
items.summary: Bessent said the Senate Banking Committee will proceed with Warsh hearings despite Senator Tillis's hold, that he proposed the committee run its own review of the Fed renovation, and that the DOJ probe's subpoenas need not mean charges. He said he expects inflation to be near the Fed's 2% target by mid-2026.
items.score_note: Mostly about the confirmation process; the inflation forecast is reported indirectly and no rate view is quoted.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post on shutdowns and interest rates
items.quote: Also, LOWER INTEREST RATES.
items.summary: Trump blamed the earlier shutdown for costing two points of GDP, said no shutdowns, demanded lower interest rates and called Powell 'the WORST'.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for lower rates.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Press conference on the Supreme Court tariff decision
items.quote: Interest rates should come down very substantially.
items.summary: Trump said the US has 'a very incompetent fed chairman who likes high interest rates' for political reasons, that rates should come down very substantially, and that the US should pay the lowest rates on the planet.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for substantially lower rates.

items.summary: Speech on economic security, supply chains and industrial policy. No Fed, interest-rate or Treasury-market content in the published text.
items.score_note: Official text with no statement on the Fed's policy rate; included for coverage.

items.quote: And low interest rates will solve the Biden created housing problem
items.summary: In the State of the Union, Trump said mortgage rates are the lowest in four years and falling fast and that low interest rates will solve the housing problem. No direct statement about the Fed or Powell was found in the transcript search.
items.score_note: Mentions low rates as a housing fix but makes no statement about what the Fed should do; scored null.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Speech on energy, Corpus Christi, Texas
items.quote: He's too late in reducing mortgage interest rates or interest rates.
items.summary: Trump called Powell 'a lousy guy in the fed', 'too late' in reducing interest rates, and said he will fortunately be 'out of there soon'.
items.score_note: 'Too late' criticism implying rates should have been cut; no explicit new demand.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Remarks 'A Reset on Liquidity Regulation' (prepared by Bessent, delivered by Under Secretary McKernan)
items.quote: After March 2023, almost everyone now agrees that operational readiness and discount window stigma need a better solution.
items.summary: Prepared by Bessent and delivered by Under Secretary Jonathan McKernan. Argues bank liquidity rules force excessive self-insurance, entrench discount-window stigma and reduce lending, and calls for counting lender-of-last-resort capacity. No policy-rate content.
items.score_note: Bank liquidity regulation and discount window design; no policy-rate content. AI tag because the text links liquidity rules to less bank lending for AI hyperscalers.
items.ai_quote: that necessarily means less lending for mortgages, small businesses, AI hyperscalers, and critical infrastructure.

items.summary: Trump asked where Powell was and said he should cut rates immediately rather than wait for the March 17-18 meeting.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for an immediate, inter-meeting cut.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post attacking Judge Boasberg over the Powell investigation
items.quote: What Boasberg has done on the “Too Late” Powell case, and many others, has little to do with the Law, and everything to do with Politics.
items.summary: Trump attacked Judge James Boasberg for blocking the investigation of Powell and the Fed building renovation, calling Powell an 'absolutely terrible' Fed Chairman guilty of 'gross incompetence, total dishonesty, or both'. No rate-path content.
items.score_note: About the Powell investigation and renovation costs; no policy-rate content.

items.quote: He should cut them right now.
items.summary: Trump said Powell is always too late and should cut interest rates right now, that the Fed should hold a special meeting, and that 'a third-grade student would know' it is the time to cut. He also attacked the Fed building renovation.
items.score_note: Explicit demand for an immediate cut and a special meeting.

items.speaker: Donald Trump

items.quote: When is “Too Late” Powell lowering INTEREST RATES?
items.summary: One-line post on FOMC decision day asking when Powell will lower interest rates.

items.score_note: Explicit view that rates should be cut now.

items.occasion: Remarks at Long Island Business Roundtable
items.quote: President Trump’s economic agenda is focused on three pillars: trade, tax, and deregulation.
items.summary: Remarks on tax cuts, refunds and small business. No Fed or interest-rate content in the published text.
items.score_note: Official text with no statement on the Fed's policy rate; included for coverage.

items.quote: by an incompetent and possibly corrupt Fed Chairman.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Semafor World Economy, Treasury Secretary Dinner interview with Ben Smith, Washington
items.quote: I think the Fed is doing the right thing by sitting and watching.
items.summary: Bessent said rates should be lowered 'eventually' but 'now ... we have to wait and see' how the Iran war affects the economy. He called the energy price shock a 'Team Transitory' case that will not get embedded in inflation expectations, said core inflation is coming down, and that he would be shocked if the ECB hiked. He said Warsh will have an open mind and will look hard at how the reserve banks are managed.
items.score_note: Endorses the Fed holding and watching for now while expecting cuts eventually; between 0 and -1, scored nearer 0.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Remarks in Washington during IMF/World Bank spring meetings week (Reuters)
items.quote: We want Kevin Warsh in as soon as possible.
items.summary: Reuters reported that Bessent was quite confident core inflation would keep falling despite the Iran war and repeated his call for the Fed to cut rates, while saying he could understand if officials wanted to watch war developments first and that it made sense for Warsh to lead the next easing cycle. The only direct quotation in the report is about wanting Warsh in place quickly. Bessent spoke at an IIF event and at WSJ Opinion Live that day; the report does not name the venue.
items.score_note: Reuters paraphrase: repeats call for cuts but accepts a pause; -1.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Invest in America Forum interview (Sara Eisen), Washington
items.quote: I think the Fed has been wrong on their inflation projections.
items.summary: Bessent said core inflation is coming down, the energy component is noise, and the Fed has been wrong on its inflation projections. He said he understands if the Fed waits on cuts 'for their own sanity' though it would not be his base case, and that waiting means they can do more later. He hoped Warsh would be in place by May 16. On private credit he said Treasury is monitoring it and convening insurance regulators, and that none of its work shows a systemic problem.
items.score_note: Still wants cuts and says the Fed is wrong on inflation, but accepts a wait-and-see pause for now; -1 rather than -2.
items.ai_quote: none of our work has shown that there would be a systemic problem.

items.score_note: Explicit demand for much lower rates, with a threat to fire Powell.

items.score_note: Rejects wait-and-see and says rates should be lower now.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview, day of Warsh's Senate confirmation hearing
items.quote: we should have the lowest interest rate in the world.
items.summary: Asked whether he would be disappointed if Warsh did not cut rates right away, Trump answered 'I would.' He called Powell 'always too late', said Warsh is 'central casting', said he has been in favor of rate rises to stop inflation when needed, but that the US should have the lowest interest rate in the world. He did not commit to dropping the DOJ probe of Powell.
items.score_note: Says he would be disappointed without an immediate cut from the new chair and wants the lowest rate in the world.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Senate Appropriations subcommittee budget hearing (Q&A)
items.quote: swap lines, whether it’s from the Federal Reserve or the Treasury, are to maintain order in the dollar funding markets
items.summary: Bessent said several Gulf and Asian allies have requested dollar swap lines to cope with the energy shock, and that swap lines from the Fed or the Treasury exist to keep dollar funding markets orderly and prevent disorderly sales of US assets. The prepared statement (treasury.gov sb0466) has no monetary-policy content.
items.score_note: Financial-stability backstops (swap lines); no statement on the policy rate.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks at a health care affordability event
items.quote: he's been terrible on interest rates because he should have lowered interest rates.
items.summary: Asked about the Pirro investigation of the Fed, Trump again attacked the cost of the Fed building and said Powell has been terrible on interest rates because he should have lowered them.
items.score_note: Past-tense criticism (should have lowered); no explicit new demand.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office remarks on Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extension
items.quote: he should have been lowering interest rates a long time ago.
items.summary: Asked whether someone other than the Justice Department could look into the Fed renovation, Trump said he has a real problem with Powell because he should have been lowering rates long ago, and that the economy is strong despite that.
items.score_note: Past-tense criticism; no explicit new demand.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post after Powell said he would stay on the Board (April FOMC day)
items.quote: Jerome “Too Late” Powell wants to stay at the Fed because he can’t get a job anywhere else
items.summary: Posted on the day of the April FOMC decision: Trump mocked Powell for wanting to stay at the Fed, saying nobody else wants him. No rate-path content.
items.score_note: Personal attack on Powell staying as governor; no policy-rate content.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Oval Office remarks at retirement accounts executive order signing (day after April FOMC)
items.quote: I think he's a negative force.
items.summary: Asked for his reaction to Powell staying on the Board of Governors, Trump said he does not care, that he predicted it because 'who's going to hire him', and that Powell is a negative force. He said the building cost angered him more than interest rates and praised Warsh.
items.score_note: Reaction to Powell staying as governor; no statement on what rates should do.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: Remarks before the EXIM Annual Conference
items.quote: Economic security is national security, and thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the United States has never been more secure.
items.summary: Speech on export finance and economic security. No Fed or interest-rate content in the published text.
items.score_note: Official text with no statement on the Fed's policy rate; included for coverage.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Speech at The Villages, Florida
items.quote: He's too late with interest reductions.
items.summary: Trump said the administration brought mortgage rates down despite 'a hostile fed guy' who is too late with rate reductions, that rates would have been even lower otherwise, and that Warsh will be a fantastic Fed Chair.
items.score_note: 'Too late' criticism implying rates should be lower; no explicit demand.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Truth Social post after the April jobs report
items.quote: more Americans are working today than ever before.
items.summary: Trump celebrated 115,000 April jobs and said the economy is strong despite the 'best efforts' of 'Jerome "Too Late and Won't Leave" Powell' and the Democrats. No explicit rate demand.
items.score_note: Attack on Powell tied to jobs data but no statement on what rates should do.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: CNBC Squawk Box interview (Joe Kernen), morning after Warsh's Senate confirmation
items.quote: I firmly believe that nothing is more transient than a supply shock.
items.summary: After hot CPI and PPI prints, Bessent said the energy shock is transient, the Fed can look through it, and core inflation was falling before the Iran conflict. He said Warsh, confirmed the night before, will bring an open mind and that after one or two more hot inflation numbers there will be substantial disinflation.
items.score_note: Argues for looking through the energy shock (against hikes) and forecasts disinflation; does not call for an immediate cut.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks to reporters (as quoted by Axios; venue not stated)
items.quote: going to let him do what he wants to do
items.summary: Told that markets now see a rate hike this year as more likely than a cut and asked whether Warsh will deliver lower rates, Trump said he would let Warsh do what he wants, that he is very talented and will do a good job. Axios dates the exchange to Tuesday, May 19.
items.score_note: Declines to demand cuts or oppose a hike when asked directly; scored 0. A clear change from his earlier demands.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Remarks at the swearing-in of Kevin Warsh as Fed Chair, White House
items.quote: I want Kevin to be totally independent.
items.summary: Trump said he wants Warsh to be totally independent ('don't look at me'), that the Fed lost its way in recent years, and that Warsh understands a booming economy is a good thing: 'just let it boom', 'we want to stop inflation, but we don't want to stop greatness', and economic growth does not mean inflation. He also praised Warsh's plans to curtail forward guidance and reform data and models.
items.score_note: Professes independence but argues the Fed should not tighten against strong growth; between 0 and -1, kept at -1 because the explicit message is against stifling the boom.

items.speaker: Donald Trump
items.occasion: Speech on tax cuts and the economy, Suffern, New York
items.quote: You get the interest rates down, everybody's going to be very, very happy.
items.summary: Hours after the swearing-in, Trump said he 'had a rotten head of the fed' and now has a great one in Warsh, that housing is all about interest rates, and that 'we're going to get the rates down' very quickly, helped by falling energy prices.
items.score_note: Wants rates down and links it to the new Fed Chair, but speaks mainly of mortgage rates and makes no direct demand for a cut.

items.speaker: Scott Bessent
items.occasion: White House press briefing
items.quote: I had breakfast with Chair Powell 41 times, and I never did that
items.summary: Bessent said he had breakfast with new Fed Chair Warsh that morning. Asked whether he pressed Warsh to lower rates, he answered that he had breakfast with Powell 41 times and never did that.
items.score_note: Denies pressing the Fed Chair on rates; no view on the rate path.

items.quote: Taken together, these efforts reflect the broader principle that President Trump has articulated clearly: economic security is national security.
items.summary: Speech setting out an economic security doctrine. No Fed, interest-rate or Treasury-yield content in the published prepared text (a fireside chat with Larry Kudlow followed; no transcript found).
items.score_note: Official text with no statement on the Fed's policy rate; included for coverage.

coverage_notes: Sources and method. Trump: (1) every Truth Social post in the window that mentions Powell, the Fed, Warsh or interest rates, read in full on the trumpstruth.org archive (timestamps are US Eastern); (2) Roll Call Factba.se full transcripts of speeches, interviews and press gaggles. Factba.se transcript pages are rendered by JavaScript, so source_url for those items is the site's own JSON endpoint that the page loads (rollcall.com/api/factbase/transcripts?person=trump&slug=...), where the quote can be matched as plain text; the human-readable page is rollcall.com/factbase/trump/transcript/<slug>/. These are third-party transcripts, labelled official_transcript only for want of a closer tier. (3) CNBC transcripts on the Versant press room. Bessent: all Treasury press releases sb0340-sb0560 were scanned by title; CNBC transcripts from the Versant press room; Reuters reports republished by SRN News (found through the site's WordPress search API for 'Bessent' over the window); Semafor. Thin spots. Bessent in March: the March 16 CNBC interview has no Fed content (only that inflation expectations are anchored) and was left out; Fox Business March 19 is covered only through a Reuters report. Bessent in May: the May 20 remarks on Treasury yields could not be opened (see unverified). Fox News, Fox Business, NBC, CBS and ABC interview transcripts for Bessent were not found as full texts, so those occasions rest on Reuters direct quotes or are missing. Bloomberg, WSJ and FT were not opened (paywall). Trump occasions were limited to those where he said something about rates, the Fed Chair or the Powell probe; passing mentions of the Fed building alone (for example March 24, March 26 Fox 'The Five', March 31 remarks, April 25, April 30 Newsmax, May 19) were not itemised. On days with several occasions (January 13, January 29, April 23, May 22) each occasion is a separate item, so same-day duplicates should be averaged before use. Scoring conventions. Posts or remarks that only attack Powell or discuss the Fed Chair choice are scored null. 'Too late' or 'rates too high' without an explicit demand is -1; an explicit call to cut now or for lower rates is -2. Balance-sheet-only remarks: the January 9 MBS comment is null, the February 8 forecast is 0 with score_basis 'forecast'. Dating notes. The CNBC Halftime excerpts page prints 'February 6, 2025' in its header but the body and video link show February 6, 2026. The Factba.se slug for the Kudlow interview ends in 2023 but the record is dated February 9, 2026. The Trump CNBC Davos interview is listed by Factba.se as airing on 'The Exchange' and by CNBC as airing during 'Closing Bell', both January 21. Discrepancy. The January 8 Bessent text on treasury.gov does not contain the line 'the Fed should not delay' that CNBC-based press reports quote from the remarks; see that item's score_note. The ai_financing tag is used twice: April 15 (Bessent on private credit, saying Treasury's work shows no systemic problem) and March 3 (liquidity rules reducing bank lending to AI hyperscalers). Neither links AI or private-credit stress to the policy rate.
